headline: Approved sewer credit, hedging policy exception, and write-offs of uncollectible accounts
summary: The commission approved a $802.33 sewer credit for the owner of 42 Washington Street after a water leak. It also approved a one-year Hedging Policy exception allowing one supplier to provide up to 42% of energy needs for 2027, and approved write-offs of uncollectible accounts totaling $232,548.01 for fiscal year ending 6/30/2026.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, including the minutes of August 18, 2026
Approved a $802.33 sewer credit for the owner of 42 Washington Street
Approved a modification of the Hedging Policy allowing one supplier to provide up to 42% of energy needs for 2027
Approved write-offs of uncollectible accounts for the Electric Division totaling $232,548.01 for fiscal year ending 6/30/2026

46 4. Discussion and Possible Action: Customer Appeal - Sewer Division - 42 
47 Washington Street 
48 
49 Mr. Langenauer stated that on April 24, 2026 the Business Office for the Wallingford Water and 
50 Sewer Divisions attempted to contact the owners of the property located at 42 Washington Street 
51 by telephone to inform them of high consumption at the property . However, a valid telephone 
52 number was not on file for the customer. As such, a high consumption notice was mailed to the 
53 owners on that same day. On May 22, 2026 the owner's son arrived at the customer service 
54 window of the Water and Sewer Divisions ' Business Office and met with the Assistant Business 
55 Office Manager to explain that an interior water pipe burst on the property and they needed to 
56 hire a company to come in and pump the water out of the basement. At that time, while speaking 
57 with the Assistant Business Office Manager , the customer asked whether they would be eligible 
58 for a sewer credit. The Assistant Business Office Manager indicated that to determine their 
59 eligibility for a sewer credit , the customer would need to appeal to the PUC by sending an email 
60 requesting the sewer credit and include any invoices and pictures that would outline the leak 
61 event. 
62 
63 On August 11, 2026 an email was received by the PUC's Executive Secretary requesting a sewer 
64 credit and included in the email were videos of the water leak clean-up . On August 12, 2026 the 
65 Business Office Manager of the Water and Sewer Divisions telephoned the customer to arrange a 
66 date and time for one of the Water and Sewer Divisions ' inspectors to go out to the property to 
67 determine if a sanitary sewer credit was warranted. On August 14, 2026 the Water and Sewer 
68 Divisions' inspector examined the property to include the water damage in the kitchen , dining 
69 area and basement and took pictures. The Water and Sewer Divisions' inspectors determined that 
70 while there were no floor drains, it would be safe to assume that while much of the water would 
71 have been conveyed to the exterior, some water would have been disposed of in the slop sink 
72 located in the basement. Based on the facts observed during the visual assessment of the 
73 property, the Water and Sanitary Sewer Inspector estimates that 25% of the potable water that 
74 went through the meter entered the sanitary system via the slop sink. The Water and Sewer 
75 Divisions' Business Manager reviewed the consumption history for this account and determined 
76 that if none of the water entered the sanitary sewer the amount of sewer credit would be 
77 $1,069.78 but since the estimation is that 25% entered the sanitary sewer system the customer 
78 would be due a credit of $802 .33 as detailed below:

101 5. Discussion and Possible Action: Hedging Policy modification to allow for any 
102 one Supplier to provide up to 42% of Energy needs for 2027 
103 
104 Mr. Hendershot referenced the memorandum from himself dated August 27, 2026 and stated that 
105 after recent discussions with Energy New England staff and Mr. Craig Kien y from Energy 
106 Initiatives, Inc ., the WED was able to fonn a tentative plan for the timing and structure of the 
107 WED's next procurement of forward energy (hedge). It is anticipated that the WED will soon 
108 look to hedge certain amounts (percentages) of its projected energy requirements for the calendar
109 years 2027, 2028 , 2029 and 2030 . During that discussion , the group identified the need to 
110 request PUC authorization to exceed the current counterparty hedging limit , as described in the 
111 captioned Hedging Policy , of 35% in any given year. Specifically, the group requests PUC 
112 approval to hedge upwards of 42% of the Division 's calendar year 2027 energy needs with any 
113 given credit-worthy counterparty. Authorizing this one-year modification will allow the WED to 
114 consider all of its available credit-worthy counterparties for the hedges needed to position the 
115 WED as described by the Hedging Policy. 
116 
117 Dr. Rinebold commented that he is in favor of giving the staff the latitude and flexibility to select 
118 some of the hedging suppliers for the year. 
119 
120 Motion to Approve a modification of the Hedging Policy and write an exception into the 
121 policy increasing the limit for anyone supplier to provide up to 42% of Energy needs for 
122 2027. 
123 
124 Made by: Dr. Rinebold 
125 Seconded by: Mr. Zabrowski 
126 Votes: 3 ayes
